title: Upload validation trusts the declared file type
evidence: Test A04-SIGNATURE accepted HTML bytes as invoice.pdf when the extension and client-declared Content-Type matched the allowlist.
reproduction: Upload non-PDF bytes using filename invoice.pdf and Content-Type application/pdf to an owned fictional ticket.
cause: The validator checks extension, length and the client-declared MIME value, but does not inspect a file signature or parsed content.
impact: A crafted file can be stored and served under a trusted-looking type, increasing content-confusion and downstream processing risk.
recommendation: Validate magic bytes or parse supported formats server-side; store the detected type and reject mismatches.

title: Uploaded files are not quarantined or malware-scanned
evidence: Static review found no quarantine state, antivirus integration or asynchronous malware scan before attachments become downloadable.
reproduction: Review TicketsController, FileUploadValidator and application service registrations for a scanning or quarantine workflow.
cause: Accepted files are written directly to the application upload volume and immediately exposed through the authorised download action.
impact: An authorised user could store malicious content that later reaches another authorised user or downstream tool.
recommendation: Add a quarantine state, malware scanning service, scan result audit event and release files only after a clean result.

title: Login rate limiting uses a shared global bucket
evidence: Program.cs registers one AddFixedWindowLimiter policy without partitioning by source address or account identifier. Test A01 confirmed the shared policy reaches HTTP 429.
reproduction: Inspect the login rate-limiter registration and send a small number of login requests from separate fictional sessions.
cause: The fixed window is global to the named policy rather than partitioned per source or account.
impact: One client can consume the allowance and temporarily affect unrelated users, while distributed abuse is not separated by source.
recommendation: Use AddPolicy with RateLimitPartition keyed by a privacy-conscious source/account composite and retain a bounded global backstop.

title: Content Security Policy permits inline styles
reproduction: Inspect the Content-Security-Policy response header returned by GET /.
cause: Inline styles are permitted rather than being restricted with hashes, nonces or external stylesheets only.
impact: The policy provides weaker protection against style-based injection and makes future CSP hardening more difficult.
recommendation: Remove unsafe-inline by moving styles to static files or authorising only required styles through hashes/nonces.

title: Application container root filesystem is writable
evidence: compose.yml does not set read_only: true for the application container.
reproduction: Inspect the app service configuration and Docker runtime ReadonlyRootfs value.
cause: The application container can write outside its dedicated upload volume.
impact: A compromised process has a larger writable surface for staging files or modifying runtime state.
recommendation: Enable a read-only root filesystem and add explicit writable tmpfs/volume mounts only where required.

title: Container runtime privileges are not explicitly reduced
evidence: compose.yml does not both drop all Linux capabilities and enable no-new-privileges.
reproduction: Inspect the app service CapDrop and SecurityOpt runtime values.
cause: The container relies on Docker defaults rather than an explicit least-privilege runtime policy.
impact: If application code is compromised, unnecessary kernel capabilities or privilege transitions can increase impact.
recommendation: Set cap_drop: [ALL], security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true], and add back only a demonstrated required capability.

title: Container base images are referenced by mutable tags
owasp: OWASP A08:2021 – Software and Data Integrity Failures
evidence: Dockerfile FROM instructions are not pinned to registry digests: FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0-alpine AS build; FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-alpine AS final
reproduction: Inspect every FROM instruction in infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile.
cause: Version tags can be repointed and do not uniquely identify the bytes used for a build.
impact: A future rebuild can consume different base-image content without a source change, weakening reproducibility and provenance.
recommendation: Pin each base image by verified digest and update the digest through a reviewed dependency PR.

title: Upload request size is not limited before model binding
evidence: The application checks IFormFile.Length in FileUploadValidator but configures no endpoint or form multipart limit near the 2 MB business rule.
reproduction: Inspect upload endpoint attributes and FormOptions/Kestrel request-limit configuration.
cause: The framework can accept and buffer a request substantially larger than the business limit before controller validation rejects it.
impact: Repeated oversized requests can consume more memory, disk or connection time than intended.
recommendation: Set an endpoint RequestSizeLimit and MultipartBodyLengthLimit close to the allowed file size, with a small multipart overhead allowance.
